title: Mock 7 · Tough Drill B
blurb: The final boss: applied numericals (NAV, bonus, STP, STT), regulatory edge cases and 'which is NOT' traps.

questions.q: A family spends ₹30,000 a month today. If inflation stays at 6% p.a., roughly what will the same monthly expenses be after 10 years?
questions.explanation: 30,000 × (1.06)^10 ≈ ₹53,725, which matches the workbook's point that expenses would cross ₹53,000 in 10 years (and ₹96,000 in 20).
hints: That is simple, not compound, growth (30,000 × 1.6).

questions.q: Assume a fund's management cost is 2% p.a. and a DIY investor could earn the same pre-cost return. On a ₹25 lakh portfolio, how much would the investor 'save' in a year by doing it himself, which must then be weighed against his time and mistakes?
questions.explanation: 2% × ₹25,00,000 = ₹50,000. The workbook's point: compare this saving with the value of one's time and the cost of emotional mistakes.
hints: That is the workbook's ₹10 lakh example.

questions.q: For a new sectoral or thematic equity scheme, the portfolio overlap with the AMC's other equity schemes (in sectoral/thematic and other equity categories) must not exceed 50%, EXCEPT with respect to:
questions.explanation: No more than 50% overlap is allowed with other sectoral/thematic and equity schemes, except large cap schemes. Sectors and themes must come from AMFI's half-yearly list.

questions.q: A Medium Duration Fund must keep the Macaulay duration of its portfolio between:
questions.explanation: Medium duration: 3–4 years, or 1–4 years under anticipated adverse situations. Medium-to-long is 4–7 (adverse 1–7); long is more than 7; short is 1–3.
hints: That is the short duration band (and the adverse range is invented).

questions.q: Which statement about a Multi Asset Allocation fund is INCORRECT?
options: It is an open-ended hybrid scheme
It invests in at least three asset classes
It must hold at least 10% in each of the three asset classes
Foreign securities can be counted as a separate asset class
questions.explanation: Multi asset funds invest in at least three asset classes with at least 10% in each, and foreign securities are NOT treated as a separate asset class.
hints: Correct choice: this is the false statement.

questions.q: A scheme has 2 crore units outstanding and its NAV is ₹18.50. What are its unit capital and AUM?
questions.explanation: Unit capital = units × face value = 2 crore × ₹10 = ₹20 crore. AUM = units × NAV = 2 crore × ₹18.50 = ₹37 crore.
hints: Unit capital uses the ₹10 face value.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the 'core responsibilities' on which trustees exercise independent due diligence?
options: Ensuring fairness of fees and expenses charged by the AMC
Personally selecting the securities for each scheme's portfolio
Reviewing the AMC's scheme performance against peers or benchmarks
Ensuring the AMC has systems to prevent mis-selling
questions.explanation: Trustees oversee; they don't manage portfolios. Security selection is the AMC fund-management team's job. The other three are listed core responsibilities.
hints: Correct choice: not a trustee function.

questions.q: Under SEBI's cyber security framework, within what time must a SEBI-regulated entity report a cyber incident by email and on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal respectively?
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates reporting cyber incidents to mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in within 6 hours and on the SEBI Incident Reporting Portal (aligned to the FSB's FIRE format) within 24 hours.

questions.q: Which statement about the onboarding of new-cadre distributors is correct?
options: They must complete KYD with biometric verification like other distributors
They are exempt from KYD/biometric requirements but must submit self-attested identity and address proof
They may sell any scheme that has beaten its benchmark
questions.explanation: New-cadre distributors are not required to comply with KYD/biometrics, but they must submit self-attested proof of identity and address. They register with AMFI in their category and sell only the permitted product types.
hints: AMFI registration under the category is required.
Only the permitted product types qualify.

questions.q: Consider these statements about FMPs: (i) Redemption is not allowed before maturity. (ii) Listing on a recognised stock exchange is compulsory. (iii) Listing guarantees that investors can exit at NAV. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: FMPs are close-ended, with no redemption before maturity, and listing is compulsory. But listing does not guarantee liquidity: trading volumes may be low or nil, and prices may be at a discount to NAV.

questions.q: How must the Key Information Memorandum be updated?
options: Once a year, within 3 months of the financial year end
At least once in each half-year, within one month of the half-year end, and filed with SEBI electronically
Only when a fundamental attribute changes
questions.explanation: The KIM is updated at least half-yearly, within one month of the end of the half-year, based on September/March data, and filed with SEBI forthwith in electronic mode.
hints: It also has a periodic update cycle.

questions.q: What must an AMC do about the unaudited financial results of its schemes for the half-year ending 30 September?
options: Host them on its website within one month and inform unitholders in writing (including email/SMS) that they are available
Publish them in two newspapers within 4 months
Send printed copies to all investors within 7 days
questions.explanation: Unaudited half-yearly results must be hosted on the website within one month of 31 March/30 September, and the AMC must send written communication (digital modes allowed) about their availability.
hints: The 4-month window is for the annual report.

questions.q: An investor wants to know the regulatory rules on how different securities in a fund's portfolio will be valued, and the rules on transfer, transmission, pledge and minors' investments. Which document should she read?
questions.explanation: The SAI covers investment valuation norms and tax, legal and general information (nomination, transfer, transmission, minors, pledge), plus constituents and investor rights.
hints: The KIM is a brief summary.

questions.q: A distributor may initiate a change of distributor code in clients' folios in all of the following situations EXCEPT:
options: Converting a sole proprietorship into an LLP
Moving clients to another distributor who offers to share a higher commission with him
Merger of business within the same group
Transfer of AUM to a close relative who is a valid ARN holder
questions.explanation: Distributor-initiated changes are allowed only for a change in name/legal status, merger or consolidation within a group, family or close-relative consolidation, and transfer of business by individual distributors. In each case the entire AUM moves to a valid, KYD-compliant ARN and the old ARN is surrendered.
hints: Correct choice: not an allowed reason.

questions.q: A distributor's data shows a portfolio turnover ratio at 2.5 times the industry average. What is the regulatory consequence?
options: The AMC must conduct additional due diligence on that distributor
The distributor must refund all trail earned
questions.explanation: Where a distributor's portfolio turnover is excessive (more than two times the industry average), AMCs conduct additional due diligence.

questions.q: Under AMFI's best-practice guideline of 12 March 2026 on the commission payout framework, how is commission paid to a distributor NOT registered under GST?
options: Base commission plus GST, paid to the distributor
Base commission only; no GST component is paid to him
questions.explanation: Commission is paid in two tranches: the base commission (exclusive of GST) to all distributors, and the GST component only to registered distributors against a valid tax invoice. For unregistered distributors, the AMC handles GST under reverse charge.
hints: GST is paid only to registered distributors.

questions.q: Scheme X gained 2.5% in its first 3 months; Scheme Y gained 4.5% in its first 6 months. Comparing simple annualised returns:
options: Y is higher because its absolute return is larger
questions.explanation: Annualised X = 2.5% × 12 ÷ 3 = 10%; Y = 4.5% × 12 ÷ 6 = 9%. Annualisation makes returns over different periods comparable, so X is better despite the smaller absolute gain.
hints: Absolute returns over different periods aren't comparable.

questions.q: Anil's NAV has fallen below his cost: he invested ₹2,00,000 at NAV ₹20 and the NAV is now ₹19, but along the way he received IDCW of ₹1.50 per unit. Has he made money, and what is his total return?
Under SEBI's benchmarking structure, which benchmark should a Fund of Funds that invests in MULTIPLE underlying schemes use?
options: The benchmark of its largest underlying scheme
questions.explanation: A FoF investing in a single fund uses that fund's benchmark; one investing in multiple schemes uses a broad market index.
hints: Applies only to a single-fund FoF (and then it is that fund's benchmark).

questions.q: A debt scheme returned 11% with a standard deviation of 3%. The T-bill (risk-free) return was 6.5%. What is the Sharpe ratio?
An investor redeems ₹5,00,000 worth of units of an equity-oriented fund directly with the mutual fund. What STT is payable, and by whom?
questions.explanation: STT on sale of equity-oriented units to the mutual fund is 0.001%, paid by the seller: 5,00,000 × 0.001% = ₹5.
hints: STT applies on redemption of equity-oriented units.

questions.q: How are gains on a hybrid fund with about 50% domestic equity taxed (units bought after 1 April 2023, redeemed after 23 July 2024)?
options: STCG 20%; LTCG 12.5% after 12 months with ₹1.25 lakh exemption
STCG at slab rate; LTCG 12.5% after 24 months
All gains at slab rate regardless of holding
questions.explanation: Hybrid funds with 35–65% domestic equity: short-term gains at the marginal slab rate; long-term (after 24 months) at 12.5%.

questions.q: In a week where Mon, Wed, Thu and Fri are business days, an investor applies to buy an equity fund on Thursday, and the money is realised and available for utilisation at 4 pm on Thursday. Which NAV applies?
questions.explanation: For equity and debt (non-liquid) purchases, the NAV is that of the business day on which funds are available for utilisation before the 3 pm cut-off. Funds came after 3 pm Thursday, so the next business day (Friday) applies.
hints: Purchases never get an earlier day's NAV in equity funds.

questions.q: An investor holds 800 units at a NAV of ₹50. The scheme declares a 1:4 bonus. What is the position after the bonus?
questions.explanation: 1:4 means 1 new unit for every 4 held: 800 ÷ 4 = 200 bonus units, total 1,000. Value stays ₹40,000, so NAV = 40,000 ÷ 1,000 = ₹40.
hints: NAV must fall to keep the value unchanged.
Treats 1:4 as 4 new units per unit.

questions.q: An STP moves ₹50,000 a month from a short-term debt fund to an equity fund. The debt fund levies a 0.5% exit load on the first two instalments only. How much reaches the equity fund in the first month (ignoring tax and stamp duty)?
questions.explanation: Exit load = 0.5% × 50,000 = ₹250. Amount transferred = ₹49,750. STP transfers are redemptions, so loads and taxes apply.
hints: The load reduces, not increases, the amount.

questions.q: A fund needs 30 days to register a SIP. An investor submits the SIP form on 20 June and chooses the 10th of each month as the SIP date. When is the first instalment?
questions.explanation: Registration completes around 20 July, so 10 July is too early. The first available SIP date after registration is 10 August.

questions.q: A folio is held jointly by Ravi (first holder) and Sunita, with Ravi's son registered as nominee. Ravi dies. Who gets the units?
options: Sunita, as the surviving joint holder (she becomes the first holder)
Ravi's legal heirs through a succession certificate
questions.explanation: In a jointly held folio with nominations, the right of the joint holder takes precedence. If the first holder dies, the second holder is substituted as the first holder, as owner and not as trustee.
hints: The nominee steps in only after all joint holders.
Not needed while a joint holder survives.

questions.q: Which of the following can be used to pay for a lump-sum mutual fund purchase?
options: An NEFT transfer from the first holder's bank account
questions.explanation: Stock-invests, postal orders, money orders, outstation cheques and post-dated cheques (except for systematic investments) are not accepted. Electronic transfers like NEFT/RTGS from the investor's account are accepted.

questions.q: Unclaimed redemption and dividend amounts are deployed in a separate plan of a liquid scheme. What is the maximum investment management fee the AMC can charge on this plan?
questions.explanation: AMCs can recover investment management and advisory fees on unclaimed amounts at a maximum of 0.50% p.a., and no exit load can be charged on this plan.
hints: Too high, and no exit load is allowed.

questions.q: A debt security written off when a scheme was wound up later yields a substantial recovery 18 months afterwards. What happens to the money?
options: It goes to the AMC's profit
It is paid to the old investors of the scheme
It goes to current investors of other schemes
questions.explanation: If the amounts are substantial and recovered within 2 years, they are paid to the old investors; otherwise they go to the Investor Education Fund maintained by the mutual fund.
